A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Revisiting Agnostic Boosting and contain readable text, equations, algorithm displays, and scientific Appendices A–E. V3 removes the NeurIPS checklist, while retaining the scientific material needed for reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports algorithms, theoretical guarantees, and proofs, with no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes in the main text or appendices. Its checklist also marks experimental questions as not applicable.

after.justification: V3 likewise contains theoretical analysis and proofs, with no original empirical outcomes in the main text or Appendices A–E.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 retain the same confidence amplification, AdaBoost updates, exhaustive relabeling, margin-based filtering, and final validation procedure. The algorithm edits concern wording and mathematical typesetting.

E1.justification: Neither version uses empirical datasets or benchmarks. The theoretical setting of agnostic binary classification remains unchanged.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates baseline methods. The same prior boosting methods appear in the analytical comparisons, including Ghai and Singh (2025).

E3.justification: No experimental protocols are introduced or revised. The algorithm's sample division, iteration rules, and use of error, correlation, and margin loss remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Neither version reports empirical ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity analyses, or case studies. The appendix comparisons of learning definitions and supporting proofs are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Confidence amplification and concentration inequalities remain theoretical arguments.

E6.justification: Neither version contains empirical scores, rankings, or observed findings. The revised sample-complexity statement in footnote 3 concerns cited theory rather than experimental results.

T1.justification: Footnote 3 changes the unlabeled sample bound attributed to Ghai and Singh (2025) from O(VC(H)/(ε^4γ^4)) to tilde-O(VC(H)/(ε^3γ^3)); the labeled bound also gains tilde-O notation. The paper's own theorem statements, assumptions, and proofs remain substantively unchanged, including the reformatted appendix equations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims: agnostic boosting under general weak-learning assumptions, nearly optimal sample complexity, a nearly matching lower bound, and interpolation between realizable and agnostic settings.

C2.justification: The explanations of the reduction and filtering mechanism, computational inefficiency, and remaining logarithmic factors are retained. The limitation stated in the removed checklist already appears in the retained main text.

D1.justification: Pseudocode and algorithm parameter information remain unchanged. Neither version provides experimental implementation, hardware, timing, or code/data access details; deleting checklist answers marked not applicable removes no actionable reproduction instructions.

R1.justification: Section 1.1, footnote 3 revises the sample requirements attributed to the already cited Ghai and Singh (2025), locally changing the characterization of concurrent work. The cited-work set and broader novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 makes local prose and punctuation edits, expands the bibliographic description of Rebeschini's existing lecture notes, and removes the administrative checklist. The scientific section order and overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Appendices B–C contain revised equation displays, fractions, delimiters, and line breaks, with consequent changes in page flow. Both algorithm displays remain, and no result figures or tables are introduced. The checklist layout is removed.

improvement.justification: V3 modestly improves readability by displaying dense calculations more clearly in Appendix B and simplifying equation layout in Appendix C, alongside fuller reference identification. The revised cited-work bound does not alter the paper's own guarantees. All scientific appendices and substantive limitations remain, so checklist removal causes no evident loss of scientific support.
